records.text: Owens said Thomas H. Patrick personally informed her by email that Kirk was lying to her about money.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Major donor was very, I thought, good to me, named Thomas Patrick. Thomas Patrick personally informed me via email that Charlie Kirk was lying to me about money.

verification.notes: This concerns a private email that has not been published or authenticated. No independent source can establish what Thomas H. Patrick told Owens or whether Kirk’s statement about money was false.

records.text: Owens said Thomas H. Patrick was Danny Phillips's grandfather.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: That is Danny Phillips' granddaddy. You know, I got to know who everybody's granddad is, and I fell apart when I realized who his grandfather was.

verification.notes: Thomas H. Patrick’s family obituary names his daughter Karen Philip and grandchildren including Danny Philip, directly confirming the grandfather relationship.

sources.title: Thomas H. Patrick obituary
sources.relevance: Names Patrick’s daughter Karen Philip and grandson Danny Philip.

records.text: Owens said Thomas H. Patrick was Merrill Lynch's executive vice chairman and CEO and worked there for 25 years in Chicago.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And I'm going to tell you more. Thomas Patrick was the executive vice chairman and CEO of Merrill Lynch. ... That's wealth management investment firm. He worked there for 25 years in Chicago. Big guy, boss, very connected, very political.

verification.notes: Merrill Lynch’s SEC filing and Patrick’s obituary confirm he became executive vice chairman and earlier worked in the Chicago office. They do not identify him as CEO; he returned to Merrill in 1982 and retired in 2003, about 21 years, and moved to New York in 1989. The title, tenure, and Chicago characterization are therefore partly wrong.

sources.title: Merrill Lynch & Co. 2003 SEC filing
sources.relevance: Lists Patrick as executive vice chairman and his earlier roles, not CEO.

sources.title: Thomas H. Patrick obituary
sources.relevance: Provides his Chicago-to-New York career chronology and 1982-2003 Merrill tenure.

records.text: Owens said Thomas H. Patrick was escorted from his office in 2003 amid accusations that he orchestrated a political smear campaign against Eliot Spitzer.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Until 2003, he was unceremoniously escorted out of his office for a scandal in which he was accused of, of all things, orchestrating a political smear campaign against Elliot Spitzer, who he didn't like.

verification.notes: Contemporaneous reporting confirms an internal investigation into whether Patrick sought to fund media content disparaging Eliot Spitzer and that he abruptly left in 2003. It also reports Merrill concluded the matter was false. The specific claim that he was escorted from his office is not supported by the reviewed record.

sources.title: Plan to Discredit Spitzer Alleged
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous report describes the investigation, Patrick’s departure, and Merrill’s conclusion that the matter was false.
